memoryReview.lesson: The instrument retains one focal shape; use one paper metaphor rather than unrelated visual panels.
Keep editing separate from the actual spatial result, but use discrete paper pages instead of a map.

references.observation: The page size descriptor controls physical page dimensions and orientation.
references.principle: Printed output needs a physical paper definition rather than screen pixels.
references.application: Generate an explicit millimetre page rule and matching proof proportions.
references.avoid: Do not rely on a browser viewport as the size of a sheet.

references.observation: Object fitting distinguishes complete content from a filled and cropped frame.
references.principle: Preserve the source aspect ratio when filling a defined rectangle.
references.application: Use equivalent cover and contain geometry for preview and PDF.
references.avoid: Avoid stretching photos independently along each axis.

references.observation: PDF viewers expose distinct page viewing and magnification modes.
references.principle: Screen magnification is separate from the document's physical page dimensions.
references.application: Keep a paper proof and display its dimensions independently of its screen size.
references.avoid: Avoid implying that the preview on a phone is physical size.

concepts.medium: Browser DOM proof and manually authored SVG contact-sheet icon.
concepts.composition: Photo settings adjacent to a literal white A4 document proof.
concepts.interaction: Commit dimensions and automatically arrange photos on paper.
concepts.motion: Immediate geometry recomposition and slight physical button response.
concepts.rationale: The accurate sheet is the primary deliverable and the visual metaphor communicates actual dimensions.

concepts.medium: Canvas-led darkroom surface with thumbnails over a black background.
concepts.composition: Large single floating photograph and a filmstrip along the bottom edge.
concepts.interaction: Move crop frames directly over images and navigate one at a time.
concepts.motion: Smooth animated transitions between enlarged photographs and the strip.
concepts.rationale: Photographic editing would be prominent but multi-photo physical sheet assembly would become harder to inspect.

concepts.medium: Text-dominant table of photo sizes and numeric output rows.
concepts.composition: Full width spreadsheet with a separate print command and no paper proof.
concepts.interaction: Edit quantities in individual cells and submit a completed batch.
concepts.motion: Focus changes and cell updates without animated transitions.
concepts.rationale: Very dense input is possible but users cannot see cropping and wasted space before printing.

selection.reason: A literal paper proof makes dimensions, cropping, and page boundaries verifiable at a glance.

rejected.reason: A photo-centric crop surface hides the spatial relationship between photos on the final sheet.
A dense numerical table sacrifices the visible page boundaries and crop preview.

tools.reason: Hand-authored vectors provide a sharp product icon without raster texture dependencies.
CSS and DOM represent physical rectangles on responsive mobile screens.

assets.role: The application icon identifies a paper contact sheet with multiple photos.
assets.acceptance: The rectangular sheet and three photo slots remain legible at launcher size.
assets.integration: Manifest and favicon point to the authored local vector icon.
assets.provenance: Original hand-authored SVG shapes, no third-party images used.

risks: Long file names and compact size controls may overflow narrow viewports.
Paper proof must remain proportional in both orientations.
comparisons: Portrait versus landscape proof after changing orientation.
Empty initial paper versus populated photograph arrangement after upload.
